blocks.title: Paint on the model, bake the map
blocks.description: Layered PBR painting, bakes and smart materials — the upstream TextureCraft editor running inside Astravia, on the mesh you opened in the workspace.

showcase.user_prompt: In TextureCraft, paint wear along the edges of @assets/helmet.fbx and bake the roughness channel out.
showcase.assistant_reply: Edge wear painted across the UV seams and roughness baked to a 2K map beside the mesh. Base colour is untouched, so the bake can be redone.

items.title: Paint on the model, not on a flat image
items.description: Strokes land where the brush touches the surface, across UV seams, so a texture is authored on the thing it belongs to.

items.title: Channels and bakes
items.description: Base colour, roughness, metalness and the rest are separate channels that can be baked out to images and handed to a renderer.

items.title: Smart materials you can trust
items.description: A smart material brings its own channels and masks, so a look is reused instead of repainted from scratch.

items.title: Wear that lands where it looks right
items.description: Strokes are painted straight onto the model, the channel is switched and the viewport is captured, so wear is placed by eye on the surface rather than on a flat map.

items.title: Install the plugin
items.description: About 9 MB of editor files arrive on first open and are reused offline after that.

items.title: Open the TextureCraft tab
items.description: Opening the tab shows the editor itself — no preparation screen, no package to fetch.

items.title: Select a mesh, then open it
items.description: File → Open inside the editor takes the file selected in Astravia.

items.title: Bake and export back
items.description: Bakes and exports travel the same bridge as saves.

blocks.content: TextureCraft is an early release: brush engines and bake coverage are still growing. The plugin runs the pinned release and adds no painting features of its own.

It paints strokes on the model and switches channels the way a hand would. Each pass ends with a capture of the viewport, so wear is reported from what the surface looks like rather than from a brush preset.
